tool: numpy 2.3.4 in Blender 5.2.2 bundled Python (system Python not used); scripts kept in the session scratchpad

method.onset_envelope: STFT 2048/hop 10 ms, 96-band mel power in dB (80 dB range), positive spectral flux at lag 20 ms averaged over bands (100 Hz envelope); low-band (<200 Hz) flux used for kicks/downbeats
method.tempo: autocorrelation of the onset envelope (50-220 BPM, log-normal prior at 120 BPM), parabolic lag refinement, then a fine comb search (+-3 %, 0.005 BPM x 5 ms phase) maximising mean onset strength on a fixed beat grid
method.beats: Ellis dynamic-programming beat tracker (tightness 100) at the refined tempo; reported first 70 s
method.downbeats: 4/4 assumed; the beat phase whose beats carry the most low-band onset + broadband onset + spectral novelty (1 beat after vs before) is the bar start
method.hits: onset peaks (+-120 ms) above the 90th percentile, score = (0.6 flux + 0.4 low-band flux) x level of the following 250 ms relative to the track max; top 10 with 1 s non-max suppression
method.drops: energy jump = mean dB of [t, t+2 s] minus mean dB of [t-2.5 s, t-0.05 s], snapped to the strongest hit within 0.6 s
method.energy: per 0.5 s block: RMS (dBFS), RMS below 150 Hz, mean onset strength
method.fit: every start offset (10 ms step) scored against the film: reveal-hit strength at 25.167 s (w2), level contrast across the reveal (w1.5), reveal hit = biggest in window (w1), correlation with a target energy curve (w1.5), 5 slams on beats (w1), cuts on beats (w0.5), hit at the 38.583 s title (w0.5), Act V lighter than Act IV (w0.5), Act I sparser than II/III (w0.5)

recommendation.start_offset_meaning: track time that lines up with film t = 0.000 s (film frame 0). Track time = film time + 32.630 s.
why: Tempo match: 120.00 BPM = exactly 12 frames per beat at 24 fps, the spacing of the 5 baked-in 2B slams (cut frames 12,24,36,48,60). At this offset every slam lands on a beat (max error 0 ms). Neither alternative can do this: masking_the_masters is 100 BPM (14.4 frames/beat, slams drift up to +-170 ms off-beat) and scifi_score is ~140 BPM with a loose grid.

Biggest moment: the track's single strongest event (57.837 s; onset strength 2.2x any other hit, +15 dB energy jump) is preceded by a 2-s suck-out to -58 dBFS. At this offset the suck-out covers the 4A cloud emergence (film 23.2-25.2 s) and the hit lands on the 4B temple reveal (film 25.207 s, i.e. 1 frame after the 25.167 s cut).
Drive: film 9.2-23.2 s sits on the track's denser tom section (13-16 onsets/bar) - the car assembly + canyon run get the busiest drumming, which then collapses into the pre-drop silence.

Ending: the same track has a sparse outro (-24..-29 dBFS) and a final impact with a 3.5 s decay; one splice at the T4 photo flash puts the outro under Act V (desk, lighter) and the final hit exactly on the 6A title.
Fit scan (every 10 ms offset, 9 weighted criteria): epical_drums_02 @32.64 s scored 5.69 vs masking_the_masters @43.06 s 4.29 and scifi_score @43.44 s 3.42.
weaknesses_and_fixes: No sparse intro (drums are full from bar 1): keep Act I sound-design only (tick bed + riser) and bring the music in on the T1 match cut (film 6.5 s = track 39.130 s), as the existing cue sheet already plans ('music drop' at T1). If music is wanted under Act I, duck it -15 dB.

Played straight through, Act V would sit on the track's loudest bars (film 32.4-38.6 s = track 65.0-71.2 s, incl. the 69.84 s accent) and the title would get no hit. Use the outro splice below (recommended) or duck -8 dB through Act V and carry the title on hit__final_title_designed.
Percussion-only: the temple's 'epic' tonal colour must come from SFX (boom__braam, choir__angelical_transition, bell__tower_toll_long/bell__gong_paiste) layered on the drop.

exact_alignment.option_exact_reveal: To make the hit land exactly on the cut, extend 4A by 1 frame (4B starts at edit frame 606 / 25.208 s; both shots have 6-frame handles). Alternatively use offset 32.670 s (hit exactly on 25.167 s) at the cost of the music beat leading every slam by 1 frame (audible flam with the slam SFX) - not recommended.
